There was a note on the mailing list about  this, "[Help Required]Unsupported routes and properties present on Redfish Interface": 

"
> *For problem #2*

> We have a use case where certain platform supports multiple redfish Chassis resource and only on few of redfish Chassis resource we want to populate Links.ComputerSystems . As per redfish schema Links.ComputerSystems is not mandatory property as for Chassis resource these are the only required fields which we are adhering to.

Yeah, I think we should use associations for Redfish Links. We have been documenting associations in PDI. I think that is a great place to start.

E.g. https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/commit/36b527af49cf87d0bc7097ea6faba4904fbf8878
"

I think we should use associations and start by documenting them in phosphor-dbus-interfaces. 
Although showing all the chassis is maybe more correct, as shown by the email we have implementations that want to be able to show chassis that belong to the system and that might not be all of the chassis. This also sets us up much better for multiple system support

Hi thanks for your info. But as what I found about associations, a system (and a manager BMC - Managers also need a link to chassis) needs to have a Dbus object path to create an association, right? I don't know if there's any other way to adhere to your method or did I miss something during investigations?

Just like we have a "powered_by" association today, I think we need an association from chassis <--> system.
https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/blob/master/yaml/xyz/openbmc_project/Inventory/Item/Chassis.interface.yaml#L54

After that is merged, this patch can look for that association
Is this using some association? Is this assuming some path ?

Hi, it's not using any association. There's currently no inventory item on D-Bus to represent a Computer System, but an Item.System interface that's attached to a Chassis or Motherboard inventory (e.g [Search result](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Aopenbmc%2Fentity-manager%20%22Item.System%22&type=code), [r200_chassis.json](https://github.com/openbmc/entity-manager/blob/430fbf69fc7d528337ac23da2da8ee610a7e4d87/configurations/r2000_chassis.json#L532)). This results in a chassis inventory appearing on D-Bus as follow:

```
/xyz/openbmc_project/inventory/system/chassis/<CHASSIS_ID>
- xyz.openbmc.Inventory.Item.Chassis
- xyz.openbmc.Inventory.Item.System
```

So, as it looks for all chassis, I let it pick up chassis that has an Item.System interface and let them be linked to the ComputerSystem.

Hello, I am currently authoring some patches regarding multi-host and also search for a solution to handle the chassis correctly. I have looked into your patch, but this approach  unfortunately would not work for multi-host. Your approach would link every found chassis to each host. Meaning, requesting /redfish/v1/Systems/{system1} on a yosemite4 server would link to chassis1, chassis2, .., chassisN. But we really would want system1 to only link to chassis1 for this specific request as per specification. I think as @gunnar@gmills.xyz already pointed out, the only viable solution would be to use associations. Since I already spent some time on this topic, I could offer to update EM to use associations for the chassis and keep you updated. I am not sure though how fast we can transition, because this change does affect every machine.. @gunnar@gmills.xyz , @ed@tanous.net is this something that should be started with a design doc?

If it helps you, feel free to write a design doc.

<gets on soapbox> For me it's a lot simpler to look at code than a design doc (ideally code that works) to check for behaviors that I can't simulate on my systems (I don't have multi-host BMCs).

You are right, the corresponding configs have not been merged yet. I just updated the configs to use the new topology port records (https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/entity-manager/+/81385). 
For now I went with 'containing/contained_by' since it is already implemented in EM. Also looking at EM configurations, xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Item.System is mostly configured in mainboard configs which is contained_by a chassis typically. I think you also once suggested a 'managing/managed_by' association which I also think is ok. I don't have a strong opinion on what the association should be called. 
I'll ping the discord thread on that one to get some better answers.

I think the best argument for `containing/contained_by` is that the Redfish data model specification uses the same terminology, expececting the Links/Chassis array to consist of Chassis resources that _contain_ that ComputerSystem.

I updated this to support retrieving linked chassis from the containing/contained_by associations between an inventory that represents the system and other chassis inventories. This is only supported for the enabling of `experimental-redfish-multi-computer-system` as the default system name "system" in when it comes to single host does not have an inventory on D-Bus to represent it. Discussion at https://discord.com/channels/775381525260664832/1385306077188460545

Why can't both multi computer system and single computer system both use the contained_by association ?
The code is updated to support both case.

@gunnar@gmills.xyz 

> Why can't both multi computer system and single computer system both use the contained_by association ?

They can, if single-host platforms migrate to use the topology design we have implemented in EM.

Also - with what we currently have - `systemName` has to be equals the identifier used on dbus for the object that represents the computer system (i.e the baseboard, but really anything that implements the Item.System interface as per PDI [1]). Currently, that seems to be difficult with default systemName `system`. It can be circumvented with BMCWEB_REDFISH_SYSTEM_URI_NAME, however I don't think, this should be the way to go.

From my understanding, if we don't put it behind the multi-host option now, then almost every - if not every - single-host platform will lose the link to chassis, that previously has been there.

So far I have seen that as a regression, which is why I suggested to put it behind the multi-host option. But on the other hand, it is a progression towards a design that already has been defined. [2] 

I would like to hear yours and @ed@tanous.net opinion on that.

With multi-host we started to introduce associations more, than single-hosts are currently using and plan on adding more. Ideally both platform types can use the same associations so that we have a single code path serving both, which I think we agree on. From past discussions at least, I got the impression, that is the direction we wanted to steer towards in bmcweb.

The way we currently implement associations however, we don't do this. [3][4] 
They are put behind the multi-host option, because most of single-host will not work as they previously did, if we wouldn't put it behind the option. 

If that is a topic that needs to be discussed in more detail, I am happy to continue on discord.
